subject: maths
chapter_title: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables

concepts.title: Graphical Representation of a Pair of Linear Equations
concepts.definition: A pair of linear equations in two variables plots as two straight lines: they either intersect at one point (unique solution), are parallel (no solution), or coincide (infinitely many solutions).
concepts.key_idea: Two lines, three stories: crossing gives one answer, parallel gives none, coincidence gives endless answers.
question_patterns: draw the graph of the given pair of linear equations and find the solution
do the given lines intersect, coincide or stay parallel - justify
find the solution of the pair from the graph
how many solutions does the given pair have - reason from the graph
form a pair of equations for the given situation and solve graphically
identify the point of intersection of the two given lines

solution_steps.explain: Plot at least two points of each equation and join them.
The intersection point, if any, is the common solution.
Parallel lines mean no solution; coincident lines mean infinitely many.

concepts.title: Comparing Ratios to Classify the Pair
concepts.definition: Writing the pair as a1x + b1y + c1 = 0 and a2x + b2y + c2 = 0, comparing the ratios a1 over a2, b1 over b2 and c1 over c2 predicts the solution type without graphing: equal first two ratios with a different third means parallel, and all three equal means coincident lines.
concepts.key_idea: Ratios tell all: both equal, third different means parallel; all three equal means coincident.
concepts.textbook_ref: jemh103.txt sections comparing ratios for consistency
question_patterns: check whether the given pair is consistent by comparing ratios
find whether the pair a1x + b1y + c1 = 0 has a unique solution
determine without drawing whether the lines are parallel
find the value of k for which the given pair has no solution
classify the given pair as consistent or inconsistent
compare the ratios and state the nature of the solution

concepts.title: Substitution Method
concepts.definition: In the substitution method one variable is expressed from the first equation and substituted into the second, reducing the pair to a single equation in one variable; solving it and back-substituting yields the solution pair (x, y).
concepts.key_idea: Replace to reduce: express, substitute, solve one variable, then return for the other.
question_patterns: solve the given pair of equations by substitution
solve x + y = 14, x - y = 4 by the substitution method
express x in terms of y from the first equation and solve the pair
find the two numbers satisfying the given conditions by substitution
solve the pair and verify by substituting in both equations
use substitution to solve the given word problem pair

solution_steps.explain: Write x or y in terms of the other from the simpler equation.
This gives one linear equation in a single variable.
Find the first variable, then recover the second; the answer is the pair (x, y).

concepts.title: Elimination Method
concepts.definition: In the elimination method the equations are multiplied by suitable numbers so that one variable has equal and opposite coefficients; adding removes that variable, the remaining equation is solved, and back-substitution gives the full solution pair.
concepts.key_idea: Add to cancel: make one variable's coefficients opposite and eliminate it.
question_patterns: solve the given pair by the elimination method
eliminate y from the given pair and solve
solve the equations by addition and subtraction of multiples
use elimination to find the fraction satisfying the given conditions
solve the pair and check the solution in both equations
choose between substitution and elimination for the given pair - justify

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the equations so one variable gets opposite equal coefficients.
Add the equations to remove that variable and solve the survivor.
Substitute back to obtain the other variable and the solution pair.

solution_template.explain: Compare with the first ratio to classify the pair.

solution_template.explain: Equal ratios point to parallel or coincident lines.
